---
title: Annotations and Spans
description: Two ways INIF labels token regions — TokenAnnotation for repeated named ranges, Span for free-form position lists.
llms-description: Annotations are named half-open token ranges with optional metadata, automatically merged when metadata matches; Spans are unordered position lists with tags and metadata.
---

INIF has two parallel mechanisms for labelling token regions, each fitting a
different use case:

| | `TokenAnnotation` | `Span` |
|---|---|---|
| Geometry | Half-open ranges `[start, end)` | Free position list |
| Identity | Named (`name`) | Named (`name`) |
| Auto-merge | Yes — same name + same metadata are merged | No — each `Span` stands alone |
| Used for | Roles, "generated", "reasoning", regex tags | Ad-hoc bookmarks, answer locations |
| Created via | `sample.annotate(...)`, [tagging helpers](../workflows/tagging.qmd) | Manual / [`create_span_from_tag`](../workflows/tagging.qmd#spans-from-tags) |

You almost always want annotations. Spans are the escape hatch for the
cases where the named-range model doesn't fit.

## TokenAnnotation

Annotations live on `Sample.annotations` as
`{name, ranges, metadata}` records. `ranges` are half-open: `(0, 5)` covers
positions 0 through 4.

``` python
from inif import Sample, TokenAnnotation, TokenOrSeqRef

sample = Sample(
    id="0",
    tokens=[TokenOrSeqRef(id=i, token=f"t{i}") for i in range(10)],
    annotations=[
        TokenAnnotation(name="generated", ranges=[(5, 10)]),
        TokenAnnotation(name="user", ranges=[(0, 5)]),
    ],
)
```

The validator enforces `0 <= start < end <= n_tokens` and rejects
zero-length or inverted ranges at construction time. Out-of-range
annotations raise `ValidationError` — never quietly truncated.

### Auto-merge

`Sample.annotate(name, ranges, metadata=None)` is the right constructor for
new annotations. It:

1. Sorts and merges adjacent / overlapping ranges in the input.
2. Looks for an existing annotation with the *same* `name` *and* `metadata`.
3. If found, extends that record's ranges (re-merged).
4. Otherwise, appends a new annotation.

This is why `tag_chat_roles_doc` can add three "assistant" annotations to a
sample (one per assistant turn) and end up with a single annotation whose
`ranges` cover all three regions.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
#### Same name, different metadata

Annotations with the same `name` but different `metadata` are kept
separate. Two `"reasoning"` annotations — one with
`metadata={"source": "reasoning_trace"}` and one with no metadata —
will not merge. This lets converters distinguish provenance without losing
the ability to query by name.
:::

### Helper methods

| Method | Returns | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `sample.annotate(name, ranges, metadata=None)` | The merged `TokenAnnotation` | Add a new range. |
| `sample.annotate_positions(name, positions, metadata=None)` | The merged `TokenAnnotation` | Add a name to specific positions; runs are auto-coalesced into ranges. |
| `sample.annotation_positions(name)` | `list[int]` | Flat sorted position list across all ranges. |
| `sample.remove_annotation(name)` | `None` | Drop every annotation with this name. |

## Span

`Span` is a flatter structure for cases where a region isn't naturally a
range — multiple non-contiguous answer positions, scoring bookmarks,
bookkeeping for downstream tools:

``` python
from inif import Span

span = Span(
    name="answer_positions",
    positions=[5, 7, 12, 13],
    tags=["mcq_answer"],
    metadata={"scorer": "exact_match"},
)
```

Unlike annotations, spans never auto-merge — adding a second span with the
same name produces two `Span` objects on `sample.spans`.

### Spans from annotations

To convert an annotation into a span (e.g. for tooling that consumes spans
specifically), use [`create_span_from_tag`](../workflows/tagging.qmd):

``` python
from inif import create_span_from_tag

create_span_from_tag(sample, "city", "answer_span")
```

The created span carries the original tag in its `tags` list and the
flattened position list of every range carrying that name.

## What annotations are used for in practice

The library's own conventions for the `name` field:

| Name | Source | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `system`, `user`, `assistant`, `template` | `tag_chat_roles` | Per-message chat-template role. `template` covers delimiters and auto-generated text. |
| `generated` | `tag_generated=True` on the Inspect / evaleval converters | The model's response — last assistant message. |
| `reasoning` | `tag_reasoning=True` on the evaleval converter | Reasoning-trace prefix of a message. |
| `special` | `tag_special_tokens` | Special tokens (BOS, EOS, etc.). |
| Custom | `tag_by_regex`, `tag_by_text_regex`, `tag_by_predicate` | Whatever you label. |

These names are not reserved — you can override or replace them — but the
[HTML viewer](../workflows/viewer.qmd) gives the chat roles stable colors so
they're easy to spot.

## Range geometry quick reference

- Ranges are **half-open**: `(0, 5)` covers positions `0, 1, 2, 3, 4`.
- Ranges with `start >= end` are rejected.
- Ranges outside `[0, n_tokens]` are rejected.
- Adjacent or overlapping ranges *with identical metadata* are merged when
  added via `Sample.annotate` or `Sample.annotate_positions`. They are
  *also* re-merged on construction by the model validator.
- Position lists handed to `annotate_positions` are de-duped, sorted, and
  coalesced into runs — `[0, 1, 2, 5, 6]` becomes `[(0, 3), (5, 7)]`.
